items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And us jazz musicians from Louis Armstrong to Coltrane to Don Cherry and Ornette and from the current day guys and Wynton and all those guys, we’ve all experienced that and we’ve all tried to sort of dampen it down with our music.

ctx.x: All right. Do you have any feeling about why in 2020, or this time in our history, that this pandemic occurred?

Yes. Because God, if you believe in God, whatever you believe, if God wants to give you a gift he wraps it in a problem. And so I think we’ve been given a gift and we’ve been made to look at ourselves and look at our actions, and we can either see and learn the lessons from those, but we’ve had problems all this whole time that we’ve ignored. And there’s a saying that says that problem that you have is now two, is now three, because you ignored it, now four because you ignored it. And it begins to grow…

your response? So one thing about artists is we do have feelings. And we express them generally through music but we also — it’s necessary for us to take a stand verbally and to language through our art but also verbally. So “shut up and dribble” that’s slave stuff. Right? When somebody tells you, “Yeah you guys get beaten when you get stopped by the police, that’s ‘cause you’re not acting like you’re supposed to act.” You know how they want you to act? Like a slave. “Yessir boss, I’s sorry. Here’s my license.”…
